tone_statements.citation: Pelkey, Jamin R. 2005. Puzzling over Phula: Toward the synthesis and statement of a sub-branch. Linguistics of the Tibeto-Burman Area 28(2): 43-78. doi 10.32655/ltba.28.2.02. Sec. 6.1 'Ani Phowa: a newly described Phula variety', pp. 58-60 (data 'adapted from Pelkey (2004)').
tone_statements.quote: Most known Phula languages have a tense-lax phonation contrast, and some retain consonant finals. Phula languages usually have five tonemes and utilize contour tonal contrasts. In spite of such systemic similarities, Phula varieties are often reported to exhibit wide lexical diversity. More Phula phonological features will be discussed in Section 7.1.1
tone_statements.n_tones: 'usually five tonemes' (Phula-wide generalisation; not a Muji-PJZ inventory)

Its Phowa sketch (sec. 3.4, pp. 9-10) is of Hlepho-FZK, a sister language; Ani Phowa-DHN (Daheineng, Xibeile Twp, Mengzi) appears only in the datapoint list (p. 3), the Phowa meso-clade section (pp. 16-17, tone-class reflexes) and lexicon footnotes. 'stress'/'accent' occur 0 times in the book.

sources.citation: Pelkey, Jamin R. 2005. Puzzling over Phula: Toward the synthesis and statement of a sub-branch. Linguistics of the Tibeto-Burman Area 28(2): 43-78. doi 10.32655/ltba.28.2.02. Sec. 6.1 'Ani Phowa: a newly described Phula variety', pp. 58-60 (data 'adapted from Pelkey (2004)').
sources.note: SILENT. The Ani Phowa sketch gives 42 consonant initials, 11 vowel finals, 'five tonal contrasts: high /55/, mid /33/, low /22/, low-rising /13/, and low-falling /21/' and a tense-lax phonation contrast; the words stress/accent/prominence/intonation/rhythm never occur in a technical sense in the whole article (stress(ed) only pp. 48, 50 non-technically).

tone.quote: Most known Phula languages have a tense-lax phonation contrast, and some retain consonant finals. Phula languages usually have five tonemes and utilize contour tonal contrasts. In spite of such systemic similarities, Phula varieties are often reported to exhibit wide lexical diversity. More Phula phonological features will be discussed in Section 7.1.1
tone.n_tones: 'usually five tonemes' (Phula-wide generalisation; not a Muji-PJZ inventory)
tone.says: Sec. 6 'Phula linguistic features' (p. 58): Phula languages 'usually have five tonemes and utilize contour tonal contrasts', alongside a tense-lax phonation contrast and, in some, retained consonant finals; sec. 6.1 gives Ani Phowa's five tonal contrasts (another variety); sec. 7 lists Bradley-style Ngwi tonal diagnostics (*H/*L 'tonal flip-flop', *1/*2 merger or split, low-falling *3) used to place Phula within Ngwi. No Muji-specific tone data in pp. 43-62.
